reasoning_summary: Round 1 uses the baseline only, since there is no prior HPO feedback. The baseline shows severe overfitting (train R² much higher than CV R²), so the grid is biased toward stronger regularization. Given the small training set (n_train=153) and only 2 descriptors, I kept the grid compact and emphasized shallower trees, larger min_samples_split/min_samples_leaf, and restricted max_features choices to reduce variance while staying within the candidate budget.
search_strategy: Compact regularization-focused grid for initial overfit correction: prioritize shallow-to-moderate tree depth, larger split/leaf thresholds, and reduced feature subsampling; include both bootstrap settings and a modest range of ensemble sizes.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Should reduce overfitting by limiting tree complexity and increasing minimum sample requirements for splits/leaves, while feature subsampling and optional bootstrap may further lower variance.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: There is some risk of underfitting because the grid intentionally favors stronger regularization, but moderate depth values and two ensemble sizes preserve some flexibility.
computational_cost_estimate: 96 candidates total; low to moderate cost for ExtraTreesRegressor given only 153 samples and 2 features.
warnings: Because n_features=2, max_features choices have limited practical diversity; feature subsampling effects may be modest.
This round intentionally avoids very deep trees and very small leaves due to severe baseline overfitting.
If CV performance drops further across this grid, the next round may need to relax regularization slightly.
